subject: Dedicated capacity — throughput targets, GPU options & budget check
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@nexushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap + a couple sizing clarifications

Alex — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and two asks so we can size a dedicated commit accurately: 

Summary from our side:
- Primary goal: replace existing hosted endpoints with a dedicated pool to meet consistent latency SLOs (95p < 300ms) for clinical summarization workflows and patient-facing chat.
- Target workload signal: ~2B inference tokens / month (you mentioned 1.5–2.5B as a range), with peak daytime load ~2.5–3x baseline.
- Preferred model family: you said generative LLMs similar to our 70B family; we used that as the baseline for bench estimates.

Two clarifying asks (if you can confirm by EOD Wednesday):
1) Token profile: please confirm avg tokens per request (prompt + response). In the call you said ~450 tokens/request average, ~1,200 tokens for heavy summarization jobs — is that still accurate?
2) Unit economics target: you mentioned looking at a committed $/1M tokens target in procurement — can you give a target range (e.g., $X–$Y per 1M)? This helps us map to reserved GPU bands.

Prelim sizing note (high level): based on the 2B/mo figure, we estimate a baseline reserved pool in the H100 band (4x H100 80GB) or equivalent A100 capacity (8x A100 80GB) to meet your 95p latency target with conservative batching. Exact bands shift based on your avg tokens/request and assumed utilization — hence the two asks above.

Sharing an initial pricing matrix (attached) with back-of-envelope $/1M numbers at a few utilization points. If you confirm the two items above, we’ll run a short benchmark using your prompt set and follow with a formal capacity quote and term sheet.

Next steps I recommend:
- You confirm tokens/request + preferred reliability/uptime targets.
- We run 48-hour benchmark on sample prompts (we can do this next week).
- We circulate a draft term sheet (pricing tiers + commit options) for legal/procurement review.

Thanks — I’m copying Marissa (pricing lead) to keep her in the loop.

Best,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147

Attachment: nexus_pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@nexushealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@nh-procure.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 09:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + a couple sizing clarifications

Thanks Jonas — appreciate the detail and the draft matrix. Answers below: 

- Tokens/request: our average across chat+summaries is ~520 tokens/request (prompt ~120, response ~400). Heavy summarization jobs spike to ~1,100–1,400 tokens; those are ~10% of volume.
- Monthly volume: we expect to hit 1.8–2.2B inference tokens/mo in year-1 of rollout (2B is a safe planning point).
- Peaks: daytime peaks approach ~3x baseline, sustained peaks during certain windows for scheduled batch jobs.
- Latency SLO: 95p < 300ms is a hard requirement for patient chat; background summarization can tolerate higher latency.
- Unit economics: procurement is targeting a committed band equivalent to ~$140–$200 per 1M tokens for contracted pricing, though flexibility exists if the committed volume / term improves the economics. For RFIs we usually show mid/low $/1M only with multi-year commits.

On GPUs: we prefer H100s if that materially helps latency; procurement is comfortable considering A100 if the price delta is significant and we can still hit the 95p target.

Priya from procurement is on copy for commercial rules and timing — she’ll want a clear doc that maps commit -> monthly cost -> $/1M at a set utilization assumption.

Could you send two concrete commit options (H100-based and A100-based) with monthly price, implied $/1M at 70% and 90% utilization, and the expected 95p latency numbers? Ideally in a simple two-row table so legal/procurement can compare quickly.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Gomez
Head of Platform Engineering | Nexus Health
alex.gomez@nexushealth.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@nexushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + a couple sizing clarifications

Alex — perfect, thanks for the quick clarifications. Attached is a concise two-option pricing sheet and a short note on assumptions (attached PDF + updated spreadsheet). Highlights: 

Option 1 — H100 reserved pool (recommended for latency-sensitive chat)
- Composition: 4x H100 80GB reserved GPUs
- Estimated steady throughput: 45k–65k tokens/s (depends on batching and request mix)
- Monthly committed cost: $62,000 / month
- Implied $/1M tokens: $31 at 2B tokens/mo (assumes 90% utilization); $44 at 70% utilization
- Expected 95p latency: ~180–280ms for the 70–90% utilization band (based on our 48h bench sim with comparable prompts)

Option 2 — A100 reserved pool (cost-first alternative)
- Composition: 8x A100 80GB reserved GPUs (approx equivalent throughput)
- Estimated steady throughput: 35k–55k tokens/s
- Monthly committed cost: $38,000 / month
- Implied $/1M tokens: $19 at 2B tokens/mo (90% util); $27 at 70% util
- Expected 95p latency: ~220–350ms (higher tail latency under peak batching)

Assumptions and notes:
- These are committed-price examples that assume a 12-month term and our managed ops. If you shift to a multi-year commit, we can tighten $/1M numbers.
- Implied $/1M is purely illustrative: final per-token economics depend on true utilization, exact model variant, and batching behavior. We’ll run a directed 48-hour bench with your prompts (we can scope this for next Tue–Wed).
- Attachments: capacity_pricing_nexus_v2.pdf (two-option summary) and a worked spreadsheet.

Requested next steps:
1) Approve a bench window (48 hours) and share sample prompts (anonymized) or a representative prompt set.
2) Priya / procurement: confirm timeline and whether you want term options (12 vs 24 months) in the draft term sheet.
3) If you want a middle-ground option (H100 with additional burst lane), we can add a third row — I can price that after the bench.

Looping Ben on the email so he can confirm GPU availability in our EU/US regions.

Best,
Jonas

Attachment: capacity_pricing_nexus_v2.pdf (PDF summary)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Nexus Health pricing ask — need quick approval for bench and pricing approach

Marissa — quick internal note. Nexus (Alex + Priya) asked for the two-option commit table (sent on 15 Jan) and wants a 48-hour bench next week. They signaled procurement target of $140–$200 / 1M tokens, which is significantly higher than our implied $/1M for dedicated commits, so commercial can structure a blended offering (hosted + dedicated) if they prefer a higher unit list for some workloads.

Ask: please confirm we can approve the bench for Tue/Wed next week and whether you want to hold any special discount authority for a 24-month term. If approved, I’ll schedule the bench and pull logs for the benchmark report.

Proposed quick decision: authorize bench + allow up to 10% list discount on the H100 option for a 24-month commit (any deeper requires your explicit sign-off).

Thanks — Jonas

(On behalf of sales ops, attaching the draft we sent to Nexus for reference)
Attachment: nexus_pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx (internal copy)
